details: The broader crypto market saw a 4.2% decline to $2.83 trillion on October 22, 2026, with Ether falling 5.4% and Bitcoin 4.0%. This downturn was primarily driven by a risk-off sentiment stemming from falling Nasdaq tech stocks, oil prices reaching a five-month high, and decreasing US Treasury yields. The sell-off was exacerbated by approximately $400 million in liquidated leveraged long positions.
title: Crypto Market Drops 4.2% Amid Nasdaq Fall, Oil Price Surge, and Broad Sell-Off

details: On October 22, Bitcoin's price slipped below $82,000, while Ethereum fell below $2,400. This decline was attributed to a selloff in US technology stocks and surging oil prices, which climbed above $110 a barrel, collectively dampening demand for riskier assets. Volatile flows in institutional Bitcoin ETFs also raised concerns about market support.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $82K as Tech Selloff and Oil Rally Pressure Crypto Markets

details: JPMorgan analysts reported on October 22, 2026, that recent actions by US regulators are partially mitigating the negative impact of the Senate's failure to advance the Clarity Act. While these measures may encourage institutional crypto participation in the near term, enduring political and legal risks will persist without comprehensive market structure legislation from Congress, as agency actions could be reversed by a future administration. The FASB is also considering classifying stablecoins as cash equivalents.
title: JPMorgan: Regulatory Actions Partially Offset Clarity Act Failure, Risks Remain

details: Ethereum developers have postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on a major test network after discovering potential security risks to existing smart contracts. The upgrade, initially scheduled for October 26 on the Hoodi testnet, will be delayed as developers investigate how a proposed gas-accounting system change (EIP-8037) interacts with current mainnet contracts. This marks another delay for the upgrade, which was previously targeted for completion by year-end.
title: Ethereum Glamsterdam Upgrade Postponed Due to Security Risks

details: Remittix has successfully raised $33 million, nearing its $36 million hard cap, with over 40,000 participants ahead of its scheduled November 24 launch. This achievement coincides with Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson's work on a new programming language for the network, which has fueled renewed ADA price predictions of $2. Meanwhile, BNB remains near $732, with supporters forecasting a long-term target of $1,500.
title: Remittix Raises $33M; Cardano and BNB Price Targets Revived

details: US spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced significant net outflows of $635.49 million on October 22, 2026. This substantial single-session withdrawal comes after DWF Labs research indicated that ETF flows typically react to Bitcoin's price movements rather than acting as a predictive indicator. The study found that average daily flows tend to shift to outflows after a 7% dip below Bitcoin's 20-day high.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See $635M Outflow as DWF Study Suggests Flows Follow Price

details: Zcash (ZEC) price hovered above $1,300 on October 22, sustaining its 15% weekly gains with three consecutive days of recovery. The cryptocurrency is experiencing renewed institutional and retail interest, evidenced by over $15 million in inflows on Wednesday and ZEC futures Open Interest reaching a 30-day high of $2.89 billion. The technical outlook for ZEC currently indicates an upside bias.
title: Zcash (ZEC) Reclaims $1,300, Gains 15% Amid Rising Institutional Interest

details: A critical security upgrade for the XRP Ledger has been postponed until November due to a voting setback within the community. This delay indicates that more time is required for consensus on the proposed fix, which impacts the network's ongoing efforts to enhance its security features.
title: XRP Ledger Security Upgrade Delayed to November After Voting Setback

details: On October 22, 2026, both Bitcoin and Ethereum are advancing with distinct approaches to developing post-quantum wallets. Bitcoin's BIP-360 (Pay-to-Merkle-Root) proposes new spending conditions through a soft fork, aiming to protect against attacks on long-exposed public keys, rather than directly introducing post-quantum signature schemes. Ethereum's programmable accounts can utilize custom verification logic, though a native, drop-in replacement for existing transaction signatures is still in draft stages for both networks.
title: Bitcoin & Ethereum Explore Different Paths for Post-Quantum Wallets
